proposal.rationale: Combines condition and intervention blocks with a Cochrane HSSS sensitivity-and-precision-style RCT filter, following the explicit permission to prioritise precision. Precision comes from community-acquired pneumonia terminology, requiring pneumonia alongside CAP, and omitting the broad drug-therapy, groups and abstract-only trial filter terms. proposal.rationale: The search combines condition and intervention concepts with an eligibility-aligned, precision-oriented randomized/placebo filter. Major-topic intervention indexing, supplemented by unrestricted title/abstract class, generic and brand terms, and mandatory placebo evidence aim to reduce retrieval toward the requested screening budget. This is a precision adaptation, not the verbatim Cochrane sensitivity-maximising filter: it can miss eligible reports lacking randomization or placebo indexing/text. proposal.rationale: This single search combines cardiovascular disease and risk populations with marine omega-3 terminology and a focused randomized-trial filter. To address the later precision requirement, it uses a narrower RCT filter instead of the sensitivity-maximising Cochrane HSSS and applies major-topic indexing to the broad omega-3 heading while retaining specific MeSH headings and title/abstract synonyms. This trades some retrieval sensitivity for precision; it is not claimed to be a validated equivalent of the HSSS. Generic fatty-acid and PUFA terms alone are omitted because they do not identify marine omega-3 interventions. No outcome, date, language, adult-indexing, or named-trial restriction is applied. Placebo and blinding are optional trial signals, with double-blind placebo-controlled eligibility assessed during screening. Broad omega-3 terminology can also retrieve plant-derived interventions, which require screening. No search was executed, as requested: fewer than approximately 4,000 records is an unverified target, not a demonstrated result. The strategy needs a live count and independent search peer review before final registration.

weaknesses_of_current: The PubMed clauses resemble selected article-title fingerprints rather than a reproducible concept-based search, creating a substantial risk of selection bias.

Neither PubMed query includes MeSH headings or adequate population and intervention synonyms.
Terms such as Cancer, Corn, Major, Adverse, events and outcomes impose incidental or outcome-related requirements that do not belong in the core retrieval strategy.
Neither PubMed query contains a systematic randomized-trial filter; title matching cannot establish randomization, blinding or comparator eligibility.
The two PubMed strings need a documented union and deduplication procedure; their separate reported counts do not establish unique coverage or recall.

The ClinicalTrials.gov condition term does not explicitly cover risk-only populations such as diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia or hypertension, and its intervention term lacks explicit drug, brand and oil synonyms.
Registered eligibility is absent, leaving cardiovascular-risk thresholds, eligible formulations, comparators and double-blinding requirements insufficiently specified.
The supplied record counts are not accompanied by exact search dates, search translations or an independently checked sensitivity assessment.

proposal.rationale: Uses antibiotic exposure as the population concept and probiotics as the intervention concept, without requiring diarrhoea, a comparator, dates, languages, or named trials. Following the later precision instruction, the trial block adapts the Cochrane sensitivity-and-precision-maximising strategy: it omits the broad drug-therapy and groups terms and restricts trial to titles. Probiotic and synbiotic MeSH headings retain full coverage; broad organism headings use major-topic indexing alongside title/abstract synonyms. Antibiotic classes, representative drug names, probiotic taxonomic variants, strains, foods, and brands supplement indexing. The approximately 4,000-record target is unverified: no search was executed, and a record count cannot be inferred from the supplied counts. ClinicalTrials.gov condition-field searching may miss studies registered only under the underlying infection; these two registry fields alone cannot guarantee complete identification of antibiotic exposure.

weaknesses_of_current: All three PubMed searches require the outcome in searchable text, risking omission of trials reporting antibiotic-associated diarrhoea only as a secondary outcome or in full text.
Explicit MeSH headings, title/abstract fields, and publication-type terms are absent; retrieval depends on automatic term mapping rather than a reproducible fielded strategy.
The trial blocks are incomplete and inconsistent. Generic control and trial terms introduce noise, while omission of publication types and relevant randomisation variants can lose eligible trials.
The second PubMed search omits the generic probiotic/probiotics terms; the third restricts the intervention to a short organism list.
Intervention coverage is inconsistent across searches and omits many renamed genera, preparations, strain identifiers, brands, and spelling variants.
The third PubMed search requires placebo, excluding eligible comparisons against no probiotic, and uses only antibiotics to represent antibiotic exposure.
AAD is ambiguous, and broad organism terms can retrieve studies unrelated to probiotic administration.

The ClinicalTrials.gov query restricts the condition to antibiotic-associated diarrhea and the intervention to probiotic, risking omission of prevention studies registered under antibiotic treatment or an underlying infection and products registered by organism or brand.
The supplied counts do not establish recall, precision, overlap, or the unique screening workload.
No eligibility criteria are registered, leaving decisions about synbiotics, fermented foods, antibiotic routes, populations, and mixed interventions unspecified.

Precision comes from requiring both population components, focusing the broad intervention MeSH heading on major topic, and using the Cochrane sensitivity-and-precision-maximising RCT filter with an additional British spelling. proposal.rationale: Combines population and intervention concepts with the Cochrane sensitivity-and-precision-maximising PubMed RCT filter, using the precision option permitted in the request. Major-topic intervention indexing improves precision, while unrestricted title/abstract class, generic and brand terms retain another retrieval route, including for unindexed records. Major-topic restriction can nevertheless miss records lacking these text terms. Cardiovascular-outcome terminology is an optional population synonym, not a required outcome restriction. Apply adulthood, placebo comparison, double blinding, mixed baseline heart-failure status and entry-population exclusions during screening; negative heart-failure or kidney terms could remove eligible records. No date, language, outcome or named-trial restriction is imposed. Apply OA-only access requirements during assessment. These searches were constructed solely from the supplied text and were not executed; a yield below approximately 4,000 cannot be verified or guaranteed.

weaknesses_of_current: The PubMed queries are fixed PMID lookups, not reproducible concept-based discovery searches; they cannot identify additional eligible publications.
Selecting particular records in advance risks selection bias and prevents meaningful assessment of search sensitivity.
The PubMed queries contain no population synonyms, intervention synonyms, MeSH terms or trial filter.
The ClinicalTrials.gov condition string does not explicitly express the eligible alternative populations with OR and may require diabetes and cardiovascular wording together.
The ClinicalTrials.gov intervention string relies on a class label and any automatic expansion, without explicit generic names, brands or spelling variants.
The reported record counts do not establish completeness or demonstrate eligibility.
The searches provide no explicit strategy for prospectively identifying newly published or newly registered eligible studies.
